gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR, which you wrote, adds a CSV export, and robin and the team acme/reviewers are also asked to review it. It covers CSV download and the header format, defers scheduled exports to acme/widgets#46, deliberately buffers the CSV instead of streaming it, and leaves the export UI to acme/export-ui.

Two problems block merging, and a required check is still running.

1. The exporter writes the CSV without its header row, so a spreadsheet that opens the file shows data with no column names. The local test export_header in tests/export.test.mjs fails because of this (src/export.ts:31).
2. The export guide says exports run nightly, but the button exports on demand, so someone waiting for a nightly file will never get one. A fix to the guide is drafted (docs/export.md:8).

maria's comment about the missing header is correct. The drafted reply agrees with her and says a fix is planned (comment-73).

The tests ran on this machine and export_header failed. In CI, the build check passed and the required unit check is still running.

Two of the three items from the earlier review are addressed. The branch was rebased onto main and pushed, one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved, and no commits were dropped.

One smaller point does not block merging: the export loop repeats the paging helper's code (src/export.ts:44). The deliver with nits option fixes it.

I recommend deliver because this is your PR and the repair can fix both problems.

Pick one:
1. deliver - fix the missing header and the guide, rebase on main if needed, watch the checks, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. deliver with nits - the same, and also replace the repeated paging code.
3. assess - post the two problems to the PR as a review and make no repairs.
4. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved on this case: both outputs satisfy all eight facts as written, so the expected plain-report/scope move (fails -> holds) does not show here. Before already described the five behaviours as functionality only in a two-sentence opening without row numbers, named no Integration entry or status, and printed the full row mapping, IDs P1/L1/P2/C1 and the 1 of 4 counters after show evidence. After keeps all of that, and its evidence response is cleaner (no echoed `show evidence` line, no `check dispositions` or `drafted payloads` fields). Three After wordings sit close to the edge and are worth tightening. First, A says the branch was "rebased onto main and pushed", but the supplied sync record has no push and the replay runs no writes; say only that it was rebased onto main, one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved and no commits were dropped. Second, the stop row now reads "remove the worktree" in A and C, where Before said "end the run without repairs"; keep that only if the skill really makes stop remove the worktree, otherwise it promises an action nothing supplied supports. Third, B dropped that the PR is approved and gained "with a message written from the spec" on the merge row; neither breaks a fact, but restoring the approval and confirming the merge-message clause is mandated would keep B's standing as complete as Before's. Moving the role and reviewer list into the first opening sentence and the sync result into the body are both fine, as long as each opening stays at exactly two sentences.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved between Before and After on this case, including scope, which was expected to go from fails to holds: Before already described the five behaviors in the opening without row numbers, printed the functionality-only row mapping, IDs and usage counters in the show evidence response, and named no Integration entry, status, latency observation or `not judged` outcome. If Before was meant to fail scope, this sample does not show it. After keeps all of that and slightly improves standing by putting the still-running required unit check into the first sentence of the second part ("Two problems need fixing before this can merge, and the required unit check is still running"); keep that wording. Three things in After are fragile even though they did not flip a fact. "No check watch has run" is an unexplained internal-sounding term in the human report, so either drop it or say in plain words that nobody is waiting on CI yet. "The spec covers CSV downloads and header format" attributes coverage to the spec rather than to the PR, so prefer "This PR covers ... as the spec requires" to keep the functionality-only reading unambiguous. "Internal verdict: fixable" and "Assessed head" should stay strictly inside the show evidence response, as they do now, and never reach the report or menu. Also keep excluding the head, prior-review and sync SHAs, CI run ID, log path and usage counters from the initial reports and the obstacle menu, as After currently does.
